analysis:
The only change in docs/architecture/inference.md is a documentation paragraph (head lines 1030-1048 per file_changes) describing a PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge. It caches token IDs of prompt pieces per prefix-cache scope, runs parallel encoding on up to four cores, applies linear-time ChatTemplateLoopRewrites for Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS, and has a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 rollback. The supplied units (head lines 1210-2012) are unchanged surrounding text, with no modifications in them. Nothing here changes code or controls.

Security-relevant claims that the next pass should verify in source, since no code was supplied: (1) The token-ID reuse is scoped per prefix-cache scope and 'never crosses a cache scope'. This relates to T-041: cacheSalt is coordinator-authored per account, model build and prompt contract. A cross-scope prompt-piece cache would add a new timing oracle or cross-account content-derived state across A-001 consumers, so scope keying must use the authenticated cacheSalt and not caller-controlled fields. (2) The cache is in-memory only, and retention, size bounds and eviction are not described. Unbounded growth or retention of prompt-derived pieces would affect T-028, T-041 and availability. (3) The four-core parallel encoding of long prompts and the sampled background comparisons with the served template are DoS and resource-bound questions. (4) The linear-time template rewrites must render identical text. A divergence could change prompt semantics. The doc says load-time and sampled comparisons disable reuse on a mismatch. This documentation-only PR cannot establish any of these as a regression. No finding is raised. Because the underlying implementation is not in the supplied evidence, those contracts are unverified. The threat model may need a note on this prompt-token cache if it keeps prompt-derived state.
